doc.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998

chapter: New York Pops and later work
title: Technology and the loss of orchestras
summary: Talkies ended pit orchestras and synths replaced film orchestras.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Technology has had such a big effect on live music over the years, from I guess when the talkies came in there went the pit orchestras for the silent movies.

And of course in film, about twenty years ago went the big orchestras. That’s why you have to thank the John Williams’ and the Elmer Bernsteins and the people who absolutely said this can not be. And it’s fascinating to me now that I go to the cinema and I hear an orchestra many, many times. Because my ears perceive that groan of that synth — well of course nobody uses, they say, that’s not chic to say synthesizer anymore. You know it’s electrical reproduction of some kind. You don’t say synthesizer.
